changes: Exact new Object[] {} and new java.lang.Object[] {} expressions can serve as auxiliary SQL metadata. They supply no first-SQL-argument, String, general constant or returned-value fact. Existing class-literal behavior is unchanged.

The constructor guard locates empty initializers in source with strings intact and verifies their masked positions. Populated string/char initializers do not become empty when literals are masked. Unknown initializers and genuine anonymous/local classes retain the guard. The original compatibility predicate remains unchanged, so newly enabled methods require complete supported statement envelopes.
limits: Only exact inline empty Object-array creations are supported; aliases, sized/populated arrays, casts, accesses and unknown wrappers remain unproved.
Helper bodies containing array initializers retain their separate conservative guard; this cycle creates no helper-return fact.
The legacy recognized-sink/local-constant enclosing-expression suppression gap remains as documented in the earlier Java SQL report. No globally sound returned-value claim is made.
The observed gain is one established negative unit, not all eight syntactic empty-array candidates. Remaining candidates have additional helper/owner barriers.
reassessment: Next, prove exactly resolved same-file private helper returns independently of opaque servlet and tainted inputs, keeping those arguments non-effectful and exactly typed. Seventeen inspected Juliet helper candidates and overlapping OWASP candidates motivate the next cycle; prospective removals remain hypotheses. Field constants had zero FPs in the inspected declaration cohort, and arithmetic ternary/simple switch support already exists, so neither is selected just to fill a cycle.
